title: add runtime NVTX counters, microbench instrumentation, and perf dashboard
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: add lightweight runtime instrumentation to make kernel, scheduler, KV-cache, and batching hotspots visible in perf dashboards and local profiling runs. This PR instruments key runtime paths with NVTX ranges and atomic counters, adds a microbenchmark harness for kernel/kv/batching scenarios, and surfaces summary metrics to the perf dashboard so we can correlate regressions quickly. Summary of changes: added NVTX scopes around scheduling, kernel dispatch, kv-cache lookup/hit/miss, continuous-batching enqueue/dequeue, and kv cache serialization points; introduced atomic counters (runtime-inflight, kv-hits, kv-misses, batch-size-histogram buckets exported via Prometheus); new microbench harness under perf/microbench that supports configurable sequence lengths, batch sizes, kv-hit ratios, and kernel stubbing to measure end-to-end latency and per-range NVTX timings; dashboard config in observability-pack/dashboards/runtime-perf.json with charts for NVTX range durations, kv hit rate, average batch size, and per-route token throughput; small telemetry additions to add instrumentation tags (model_id, route, quant_profile) to metrics. Commits (high level): - Add NVTX scopes and helper macros in runtime/instrumentation - Export runtime counters via prometheus client in runtime/metrics - Microbench harness and regression test harness perf/microbench - Dashboard and grafana panels in observability-pack/dashboards - Unit tests and CI tweaks to enable perf microbench job in CircleCI - Docs: add instrumentation guide to docs/observability/instrumentation.md Files changed (high level): runtime/instrumentation/nvtx.hpp, runtime/instrumentation/nvtx.cpp, runtime/metrics/prometheus_exporter.cpp, runtime/scheduler/scheduler.cpp (added NVTX ranges around schedule loop), runtime/kv/kv_cache.cpp (added counters and NVTX on lookup), runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.cpp (NVTX and batch-size metrics), perf/microbench/kv_kernel_bench.py, perf/microbench/README.md, observability-pack/dashboards/runtime-perf.json, docs/observability/instrumentation.md, ci/circleci-perf.yml, tests/microbench/test_kv_bench.py Review notes and conversation: - Priya: requested clearer naming for NVTX ranges to include model and route; also requested atomic counters to be 64-bit. Author: updated macros to include model/route tags where available and switched counters to uint64_t. - Ethan: asked for low-overhead default (disabled metrics by default). Author: metrics and NVTX are opt-in via runtime flags (--enable-instrumentation) and build flag (INSTRUMENTATION=ON). - Lena: requested a dashboard panel showing kv hit-rate over time and example thresholds. Author: added kv hit-rate panel and notes in dashboard JSON. CI and testing: Added a dedicated perf job that runs microbench against a small local runtime/docker image in CircleCI. First CI run had a lint failure (nvtx include missing guard) that was fixed in follow-up commit; final CI status: pass. Local validation: ran microbench with 10k iterations across batch sizes [1,4,8,16] and sequence lengths [64,512]; collected NVTX traces and validated ranges are correctly nested. Example microbench summary (local): - median end-to-end token latency (batch=1, seq=64): 8.6 ms - median token latency (batch=8, seq=64): 3.1 ms - kv-cache hit-rate (simulated 80%): 78.9% (counts match exported counters) Backwards compatibility and risk: all instrumentation disabled by default; enabling adds minimal overhead (lightweight NVTX ranges and atomic counters). No API breaking changes. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable perf microbench job behind a circleci flag, iterate on dashboards with SRE. Merge: squash-merged after approvals. Follow-ups planned: - Wire NVTX -> distributed trace correlation for end-to-end request tracing (ENG-8020) - Add microbench regression gating to CI for prioritized routes (ENG-7891)

notes: This PR is primarily instrumentation; no production performance changes expected when disabled. The microbench harness will be used to create regression thresholds in follow-up work.
